answer: No. In thread t0630 ("ISSUE: P62 needs a parent and a sibling", July 2012), Vladimir Alexiev proposed adding physical-domain shortcut siblings of P62_depicts — tentatively numbered P67a and P129a — to let a physical object directly 'refer to' (parallel to P67_refers_to) or be 'about' (parallel to P129_is_about) something, mirroring how P62 shortcuts P138_represents. Stephen Stead, Matthew Stiff and Sebastian Rahtz debated examples (blue plaques, gravestone epitaphs, a drawing referencing a scriptwriter), and Martin Doerr gave a detailed theoretical rebuttal arguing that unlike depiction, textual/inscribed 'aboutness' usually passes through an intermediate object (e.g. an inscription) that has its own documentary identity, so shortcutting over it would be counterproductive to information integration; he said CRM-SIG would need to consider the new evidence at a future meeting. No such properties were ever added: the archive's own chronology for P62 tags this episode as 'unresolved', and the current ontology skeleton (v7.1.3) still shows P67 and P129 with only E89 Propositional Object as domain — no E24 Physical Human-Made Thing siblings exist. So the parallel shortcut proposal was discussed but not accepted.
